Just days after kicking off the public beta season and rolling out a revised macOS 27 developer beta 3, Apple is back with macOS 27 developer beta 4. Here's what you need to know.

Apple Rolls Out macOS 27 Beta 4

Last week, Apple released macOS 27 public beta 1, which carried the same build number as a revised version of macOS 27 developer beta 3 that shipped around the same time.

That means, unless there's a major issue, today's developer release will likely arrive as macOS 27 public beta 2 in the coming days.

macOS 27 developer beta 3 fixed some stability issues introduced by macOS developer beta 2 and added new Golden Gate Bridge-themed wallpapers and screensavers, as Apple continues preparing for the official release later this year.

macOS 27 Golden Gate brings a number of refinements to Liquid Glass, including a new slider that lets you dial in exactly how transparent or opaque you want interface elements. It also unifies the rounded corner design across system windows, apps, and software, addressing a much-maligned issue in macOS 26.

Additionally, macOS 27 Golden Gate ships with an all-new Siri AI and its companion app, which uses a fresh underlying indexing system to more precisely pull in relevant information to ground Siri's generated answers. Siri AI, and macOS 27 Golden Gate as a whole, run on third-generation Apple Foundation Models, which you can read more about here.

macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 4 carries a build number of 26A5388g. We're digging through the new beta now and will report back on what we find.

macOS 27 Golden Gate Beta 4 Is Now Available

Here's how to install the macOS 27 Golden Gate developer beta 4:

  • Back up your Mac
  • Open System Settings
  • Go to General → Software Update
  • Click the "i" next to Beta Updates
  • From the drop-down in the upper-right corner, choose macOS Developer Golden Gate Beta
  • Press Done

Did you find anything new in macOS 27 Golden Gate beta 3? Let us know in the comments.
